rationale: The Court is most likely to issue a narrow, precedent-respecting opinion holding that § 1983 remains available for Spending Clause statutes when (and only when) the particular FNHRA provisions unambiguously confer resident-specific rights under Gonzaga and are not displaced by a comprehensive, exclusive remedial scheme. Separate writings are most likely from Justice Thomas (and possibly Justice Alito) pressing the Spending Clause/Armstrong structural objection, and from one or more majority justices to emphasize the decision’s provision-by-provision limits.
